mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the UNRATE increase does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 800,000 units signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the decline in HOUST does not correlate with broader economic slowdown indicators.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 2% MoM signals strengthening economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the INDPRO increase does not correlate with broader economic growth indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real final sales (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over the past quarter, it signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in past quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS growth exceeding GDPC1 growth does not correlate with subsequent economic strength.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of rising UNRATE and falling PAYEMS does not correlate with broader economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals tightening supply conditions and inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of INDPRO growth and rising FEDFUNDS does not correlate with subsequent economic tightening.
